claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. My child's name is Alex and they're 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and Alex's situation.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand more about your responsibility for Alex.

**Does Alex normally live with you, and are you responsible for them? This means you're responsible for things like their day-to-day care, their upbringing, and their financial support.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home and I'm responsible for their day-to-day care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about Alex's education and work situation, as this is important for determining eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, or have they left education? If they're in education, what type (for example, school, college, sixth form)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is still in school - they're doing their GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- Married or in a civil partnership?
- Receiving certain benefits in their own right (like Universal Credit or Income Support)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't married or in a civil partnership, and they don't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is there anyone else who also claims Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else also responsible for them in the same household (such as another parent or partner)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £50,000 per year? This is important because it may affect whether you need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge, though it doesn't affect your eligibility to claim.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into my income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to find out if I'm eligible to claim in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex (age 15) who lives with you
- Alex is in full-time education (doing GCSEs at school)
- Alex is under 16 years old
- Alex is not married or in a civil partnership
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. Children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training, qualify for Child Benefit when someone is responsible for them.

Let me provide you with the formal assessment now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You can proceed with making a claim if you haven't already. Just be aware that if you or your partner's individual income is over £50,000, you may need to pay a High Income Child Benefit Charge through your tax return, though you're still entitled to claim the benefit itself.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
